extracted.intended_audience: Small business applicants preparing NIAID SBIR (NIAID-AT-SBIR R43/R44) grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and assembling a Phase II SBIR application to NIAID (advanced technology FOA) including required forms, project narrative, human subjects documentation, budgets, commercialization plan, and consortium agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow funding opportunity (FOA) instructions / application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications

rubrics_metrics.name: SF 424 (R&R) Face Page / Applicant Information completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide required SF 424 (R&R) items: Type of Submission, Federal Identifier, Applicant Organizational DUNS, Legal Name, Department/Division, Street/City/State/ZIP/Country, Project Title, Proposed Project Start and End Dates, Type of Applicant, Employer Identification (EIN/TIN), Congressional District, Contact person for matters involving the application, and other standard SF424 fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all mandatory fields are filled (e.g., DUNS, EIN), include accurate PD/PI contact information, and include signatures/certifications. The application includes checkboxes for New/Resubmission/Renewal/Continuation/Revision and fields about program income and state review (EO 12372).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications and Assurances / Authorized Representative signature
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, an authorized representative certifies to the statements in the list of certifications and provides required assurances and agrees to comply with resulting award terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signature acknowledges awareness of penalties for false statements (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001). Provide authorized representative name, title, organization, contact info and date signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract (Description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a concise Project Summary/Abstract describing the research goals, significance and approach (e.g., need for the assay, limitations of current methods, proposed transformation to a field-usable rapid test).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize importance to monitoring/preventing the health problem and the planned approach; keep it clear and focused as a standalone summary for reviewers and program staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Relevance Statement (narrative attachment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a separate Public Health Relevance Statement describing the public health importance of the proposed project in plain language (e.g., why a rapid HIV incidence test is essential for epidemic monitoring and prevention).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the project will impact public health practice and surveillance in field conditions; keep language accessible to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe scientific environment and available resources: laboratory, clinical, animal, computer, office, other support, and major equipment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail capabilities (e.g., instrumentation, clean rooms, dry rooms, biosafety cabinets, freezers), space (square footage), certifications (ISO, EN), supporting staff availability, and any unique institutional resources. Indicate clinical or animal facility availability or absence. Explain how these resources support the proposed work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research & Related Senior/Key Person Profiles and Biographical Sketches
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide biographical sketches for each listed Senior/Key Person following the PHS 398 format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include Personal Statement, Education/Training, Positions and Honors, Relevant Publications, and other required sections. Explicit instruction: 'BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FOUR PAGES.' Attach current & pending support as requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget Forms and Budget Justification (Research & Related Budget)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed budgets for each year (Year 1, Year 2, Year 3, etc.), cumulative budget, and consortium/subaward budgets as applicable, along with a Budget Justification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show subtotal direct costs (excluding consortium F&A where noted), total federal and non-federal funds, anticipated program income (if any), and adhere to FOA rules on allowable costs and caps. Include documentation for consortium budgets (subaward 1, 2, 3) and supporting justification for personnel, equipment, supplies, travel, and subcontracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercialization Plan (SBIR/STTR Information)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an SBIR/STTR Commercialization Plan describing plans to move the innovation to market, commercialization strategy, and any prior SBIR Phase II awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For SBIR applications, include realistic commercialization milestones, market analysis, regulatory pathway considerations, manufacturing and distribution plans, and any prior phase awards or commercialization achievements. Table of Contents shows 'Commercialization Plan' and 'Prior SBIR Phase II Awards' sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a Specific Aims page that clearly states the aims of the proposed research and the objectives to be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be focused, testable, and linked to the overall goal. The Table of Contents shows Specific Aims as a distinct required section (page 115).

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan: Research Strategy (Approach, Significance, Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the Research Strategy including background/significance, innovation, and detailed approach/methods to accomplish the specific aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe proposed methods, anticipated results, feasibility and preliminary data, potential problems and alternative approaches, and how the project addresses significance and innovation. Provide sufficient methodological detail for reviewers to assess rigor and feasibility. (Research Strategy listed starting page 116.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects Protections and Related Sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete Human Subjects sections including Protection of Human Subjects, Women & Minorities, Planned Enrollment Table, Children, and indicate whether human subjects are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide IRB approval date and Human Subject Assurance Number where applicable, indicate whether the project is exempt (and which exemption), include details on protections, inclusion plans for women/minorities/children, planned enrollment numbers, and clarify whether the project involves a clinical trial (table shows 'Clinical Trial: N'). If humans are involved, answer required questions (Is the Project Exempt? If yes, specify exemption number).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals / IACUC documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If vertebrate animals are used, provide IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number and answer related questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate whether IACUC review is pending, provide species and justifications, and supply necessary documentation for animal welfare compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Attachments (Supplementary documentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include any other required attachments listed by the FOA (e.g., institutional letters, specific attachments like 'Sbc 000001387').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'Other Attachments' section to provide documents requested by the FOA or that support compliance (e.g., institutional approvals, data use agreements, sample panels). Maintain clear filenames and attach appropriately to the corresponding form fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography & References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a complete Bibliography & References Cited section supporting the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite relevant literature referenced in the Research Plan and elsewhere; include full citations. Table of Contents indicates location (page 133).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortium / Contractual Arrangements
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe consortium roles, responsibilities, division of work, financial arrangements, and dispute resolution for all consortium partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which organization will administer the grant, responsibility for site finances and work products, accounting/audit compliance, how disagreements will be handled (good faith discussions; PI decision if necessary), and specifics of technology sharing or in-kind participation (e.g., CDC providing services at its own expense). Include letters of support or subaward documentation as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach Letters of Support from collaborators, consultants, or partner organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should document commitment, describe roles/contributions, and clarify any in-kind or IRB/field support. Place in the Letters of Support section (page indicated in Table of Contents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide plans for sharing data, resources, reagents, and other outputs developed under the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe how data and resources will be made available (e.g., repositories, sharing schedules), any restrictions, and compliance with NIH resource sharing policies. Place in the Resource Sharing Plan section (page 147).

rubrics_metrics.name: PHS 398 Checklist items (application administrative compliance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete the PHS 398 Checklist addressing application type, change of investigator/institution, inventions and patents, program income, and disclosure permission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer checklist items truthfully. For inventions/patents indicate if previously reported. For program income, if anticipated, provide budget periods, amounts, and sources. For disclosure permission, state whether the Government may disclose applicant contact information if the application is not awarded. Follow PHS 398 instructions (pages 148-149).

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA, Copyright, and Accessibility statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge copyright terms and FOIA implications and ensure Section 508 accessibility conformance as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIAID notes that application text is copyrighted and posted with permission for nonprofit educational use only (material must remain unchanged and credit investigators/organizations). FOIA requests will be subject to exemptions and may include substantial redactions for confidential commercial/financial information, reviewer comments, deliberations, and personal privacy. For accessibility issues contact the NIAID Office of Knowledge and Educational Resources (deaweb@niaid.nih.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Performance Sites and Contact Information
rubrics_metrics.description: List research performance sites and ensure accurate contact and organizational information for applicant and PD/PI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include street addresses, city/state/ZIP, phone/fax numbers, organizational names, and indicate whether the performance site is eligible to be designated as historic if relevant. Ensure congruence between SF424 face page and supplemental contacts.
